title: Response to DRC's Ebola Epidemic Hampered by Funding Shortfall and Misinformation, Frontline Workers Say
detail: The Washington Post reported on 26 August 2026 that the response to DRC's 'raging' Ebola epidemic has been hampered by a severe lack of funding and pervasive misinformation, according to people working on the front lines — echoing UN Senior Ebola Coordinator Julien Harneis's 21 August warning that response funding 'will run out' within weeks. The report comes as the outbreak, already the largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic in DRC's history, continues spreading through communities also facing conflict, displacement and food insecurity, with rumors and vaccine skepticism undermining case-finding and community cooperation even as case counts pass 5,500 confirmed and over 2,600 deaths.

title: DRC Case Count Reaches 5,713 as CFR Climbs to Nearly 48%, ECDC Tracker Shows
detail: ECDC's Ebola outbreak tracker, updated 26 August 2026 with data through 25 August, recorded 5,713 confirmed DRC cases and 2,744 deaths — a single-day increase of 57 cases and 29 deaths — with 770 patients hospitalized in isolation, 1,269 recovered, and 84.6% of identified contacts under active follow-up. Ituri province remained the epicenter with 4,750 cases and 2,133 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones, followed by North Kivu (753 cases/512 deaths), Haut-Uélé (189/89), Tshopo (15/8), South Kivu (3/1) and Bas-Uélé (3/1) — 58 of DRC's 151 health zones now affected across six provinces. A Forbes analysis published 27 August by epidemiologist John Drake put the crude CFR at nearly 48% (up from 45.6% earlier in the outbreak), cited 160 healthcare-worker infections with 44 deaths (~29% CFR), and estimated true infections could be running 8,600-10,300 given case-detection gaps, while arguing the outbreak — despite record scale — remains controllable with adequate resources, citing Uganda's successful containment of the same strain.
